titleStmt.title: Formation of short chain fatty acids by the gut microbiota and their impact on human metabolism
titleStmt.author: Douglas J. Morrison
Tom Preston

publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Formation of short chain fatty acids by the gut microbiota and their impact on human metabolism

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: short chain fatty acids as signalling molecules between the gut microbiota and human metabolism
span.quote: Short chain fatty acids (SCFA) are the primary end-products of fermentation of non-digestible carbohydrates (NDC) that become available to the gut microbiota. They represent the major flow of carbon from the diet, through the microbiome to the host.

span.label: whether short chain fatty acids are the key molecular link between diet, the microbiome and host health, and what the evidence for that actually supports
span.quote: _Is the microbiome a passive substrate-degrading system or are signaling molecules actively involved in microbiome-host “crosstalk”?_ Undoubtedly the answer to this quandary is yes, the molecules produced through microbiota activity provide important regulatory signals to the host and in the “-omics” revolution, metabolomics is a key enabling technology which will enable the identification of the repertoire of signals between microbiome and host.

span.label: an integrated review of SCFA across gut, liver and periphery which states, as its own finding, that the field has no method to measure SCFA production in humans and that the animal doses behind its mechanisms are far above habitual human intake
span.quote: The field has been hampered by a lack of methodology to measure SCFA production directly in human studies, although recent work suggests that stable isotope techniques may hold promise. 18 Observations in humans have largely relied on the measurement of stool SCFA output, although it is unclear whether stool SCFA output is a suitable proxy for luminal SCFA production.

span.label: mechanism
span.quote: These observations suggest that the roles of SCFA should be considered in each cell or tissue type within this biological gradient. The interplay between epithelial utilization and integrity, splanchnic utilization and peripheral availability requires delineation to determine whether increased production of all SCFA, or selective increases in individual SCFA at specific tissues, determines some of the observed metabolic effects.

span.label: SCFA produced by saccharolytic fermentation in the colon act on gut epithelium, liver and peripheral tissues along a falling concentration gradient
span.quote: There is a strong biological gradient for each SCFA from the gut lumen to the periphery which leads to differing cell and tissue SCFA exposure

span.label: narrative review of human and animal evidence, with the animal fibre loadings converted to human dry-matter-intake equivalents using the UK National Diet and Nutrition Survey
span.term: narrative review of human and animal evidence, with the animal fibre loadings converted to human dry-matter-intake equivalents using the UK National Diet and Nutrition Survey
span.quote: Thus translating the fiber supplementation rates from animal experiments, a daily fiber supplementation in the range 20.9 – 83.7 g/d for men and 16.3 – 65.3 g/d of dietary fiber would be broadly comparable with the 5 – 20% w/w diet loadings used in animal studies.

span.label: butyrate raises intestinal barrier integrity by increasing claudin-1 and ZO-1 expression and redistributing occludin - the tight junction proteins
span.quote: Of the SCFA produced in the colon, butyrate appears to be the most important regulator of TJP and has been shown to enhance intestinal barrier function through increased expression of claudin-1 and Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1) and occludin redistribution; proteins which are critical components of the tight junction assembly.

span.label: in the liver propionate is gluconeogenic while acetate and butyrate are lipogenic, so the propionate:acetate ratio determines how much colonic carbon reaches lipid stores
span.quote: In the liver, propionate is gluconeogenic while acetate and butyrate are lipogenic.

span.label: butyrate is the preferred fuel of the colonocyte and the gut epithelium is where it is sequestered - the paper's own reason for the steep epithelial step in the gradient
span.quote: It is well established that SCFA, and butyrate in particular, are important substrates for maintaining the colonic epithelium. Butyrate is the preferred fuel utilised by coloncytes and the primary site of butyrate sequestration in the body is the gut epithelium.

span.label: THE PAPER NAMES ITS OWN MECHANISM'S EXCEPTION IN THE NEXT SENTENCE: the `butyrate paradox` - proliferation in healthy colonocytes, apoptosis in transformed ones - is followed immediately by a mouse model where butyrate fuels hyper-proliferation in MSH2-deficient cells and enhances tumour formation
span.quote: However, in a mouse model of colorectal cancer, butyrate appears to fuel hyper-proliferation in MSH2 deficient colon epithelial cells leading to enhanced tumor formation.

span.label: THE FIELD HAS NO METHOD TO MEASURE ITS PRIMARY VARIABLE: SCFA production cannot be measured directly in humans, and it is unclear whether stool SCFA output - what is measured instead - is a suitable proxy for luminal production
span.quote: The field has been hampered by a lack of methodology to measure SCFA production directly in human studies, although recent work suggests that stable isotope techniques may hold promise. 18 Observations in humans have largely relied on the measurement of stool SCFA output, although it is unclear whether stool SCFA output is a suitable proxy for luminal SCFA production.

span.label: the appetite-regulation mechanism cannot be attributed to SCFA at all until such a method exists, which the authors state as a condition rather than a caveat
span.quote: Whether these high fiber intakes elicit their appetite-regulating effects via SCFAs and FFAR 2/3 signaling pathways awaits a method to quantify SCFA production _in vivo_.

span.label: the human evidence is associative rather than interventional, so high-level evidence from controlled trials is largely lacking
span.quote: However, high-level evidence from controlled human trials supporting SCFA as key regulation factors in human metabolism is largely lacking and there is significant reliance on associative studies, rather than interventional studies.

span.label: there is insufficient evidence to inform any evidence-based clinical or public health intervention using SCFA formulations - stated in the paper's own introduction
span.quote: However, at the present time, there is insufficient evidence to inform appropriate, evidence-based clinical or public health interventions with clearly defined outcomes using SCFA formulations.

span.label: whether oral SCFA feeding in animals, which produces circulating concentrations far above the human normal range, is an appropriate model for human SCFA physiology requires further validation
span.quote: Whether oral SCFA feeding studies that lead to high circulating SCFA concentration in animals, particularly propionate, represent an appropriate model for human SCFA physiology requires further validation.

span.label: whether SCFA play an important role in mucosal maintenance and integrity in HUMAN models is stated by the authors as urgently needing further work
span.quote: Further work is urgently needed in human models to determine whether SCFA play an important role in mucosal maintenance and integrity.

span.label: dry matter intake, a livestock-nutrition unit, used to convert rodent dietary fibre loadings into a comparable human daily intake
span.quote: Animal studies which use dietary fiber supplementation to manipulate colonic SCFA tend to use relatively high fiber supplementation; 5 – 20% w/w NDC in animal dry matter intake (DMI).

span.label: the animal fibre dose is converted to a human-equivalent intake using national survey data before the animal findings are used
span.note: eliminates: an effect produced only by a dose no human diet reaches being read as a statement about human physiology · outcome: failed
span.quote: Thus translating the fiber supplementation rates from animal experiments, a daily fiber supplementation in the range 20.9 – 83.7 g/d for men and 16.3 – 65.3 g/d of dietary fiber would be broadly comparable with the 5 – 20% w/w diet loadings used in animal studies.

span.label: circulating SCFA concentrations in oral-feeding animal models are compared with the human normal range
span.note: eliminates: a concentration that is pathological in humans being treated as the physiological range · outcome: failed
span.quote: High circulating concentrations of SCFA (>1mmol/L; normal range, 0–5 μmol/L for propionate and butyrate), other than acetate, are observed in acidaemic disease in humans and have profound impacts on metabolism because of the toxicity of these organic acids at high concentrations.

span.label: the size of colonic propionate production is set against endogenous glucose production before propionate is called gluconeogenic at the whole-body level
span.note: eliminates: a real but negligible flux being reported as a contributor to glucose homeostasis · outcome: held
span.quote: From stoichiometric equations of daily SCFA production from dietary fiber intake, 42 daily propionate production, estimated to be 29.5 mg/kg/day for an average 85 kg human, is likely to make only a relatively small contribution to endogenous glucose production (2.2 mg/kg/min 43) of which approximately 50% may be attributable to gluconeogenesis.

span.label: SCFA
span.quote: SCFA are produced mainly through saccharolytic fermentation of carbohydrates that escape digestion and absorption in the small intestine and the pathways of SCFA production are relatively well understood 4 and recently described in detail. The major products are formate, acetate, propionate and butyrate.

span.label: butyrate
span.quote: It is well established that SCFA, and butyrate in particular, are important substrates for maintaining the colonic epithelium. Butyrate is the preferred fuel utilised by coloncytes and the primary site of butyrate sequestration in the body is the gut epithelium.

span.label: propionate
span.quote: In the liver, propionate is gluconeogenic while acetate and butyrate are lipogenic.

span.label: biological gradient
span.quote: There is a strong biological gradient for each SCFA from the gut lumen to the periphery which leads to differing cell and tissue SCFA exposure

span.label: cross-talk
span.quote: 3) improvements in our understanding of the intricate molecular signaling (referred to as “cross-talk”) between the gut microbiome and the host.

span.label: molecular signaling
span.quote: 3) improvements in our understanding of the intricate molecular signaling (referred to as “cross-talk”) between the gut microbiome and the host.

span.label: acetate
span.quote: In the liver, propionate is gluconeogenic while acetate and butyrate are lipogenic.

span.label: intestinal barrier function
span.quote: Of the SCFA produced in the colon, butyrate appears to be the most important regulator of TJP and has been shown to enhance intestinal barrier function through increased expression of claudin-1 and Zonula Occludens-1 (ZO-1) and occludin redistribution; proteins which are critical components of the tight junction assembly.

span.label: high-fiber diets
span.quote: A number of studies have advanced the “energy harvesting” hypothesis, whereby SCFA are thought to contribute additional calories through fermentation in the obese as an explanation for additional weight gain. However, this is not supported by the observational evidence in humans where high-fiber diets, which would be expected to increase SCFA production, protect against weight gain.

span.label: energy harvesting
span.quote: A number of studies have advanced the “energy harvesting” hypothesis, whereby SCFA are thought to contribute additional calories through fermentation in the obese as an explanation for additional weight gain. However, this is not supported by the observational evidence in humans where high-fiber diets, which would be expected to increase SCFA production, protect against weight gain.

span.label: SCFA - AS DEFINED HERE: the primary end-products of fermentation of non-digestible carbohydrate that reach the gut microbiota, and the major flow of carbon from the diet through the microbiome to the host
span.quote: Short chain fatty acids (SCFA) are the primary end-products of fermentation of non-digestible carbohydrates (NDC) that become available to the gut microbiota. They represent the major flow of carbon from the diet, through the microbiome to the host.

span.label: SCFA production - the quantity every claim in this literature is about, and the one with no method behind it in humans; STOOL SCFA OUTPUT is what is measured and its adequacy as a proxy is explicitly unsettled
span.quote: The field has been hampered by a lack of methodology to measure SCFA production directly in human studies, although recent work suggests that stable isotope techniques may hold promise. 18 Observations in humans have largely relied on the measurement of stool SCFA output, although it is unclear whether stool SCFA output is a suitable proxy for luminal SCFA production.

span.label: the biological gradient - SCFA concentration falling from gut lumen to periphery, so `an SCFA effect` is not one quantity but a different exposure in every tissue
span.quote: There is a strong biological gradient for each SCFA from the gut lumen to the periphery which leads to differing cell and tissue SCFA exposure

span.label: critiques → the animal SCFA literature, on the ground that its fibre loadings translate to 20.9-83.7 g/d for men against a habitual UK intake of 14.7 g/d
span.quote: Thus translating the fiber supplementation rates from animal experiments, a daily fiber supplementation in the range 20.9 – 83.7 g/d for men and 16.3 – 65.3 g/d of dietary fiber would be broadly comparable with the 5 – 20% w/w diet loadings used in animal studies. Also from UK NDNS data, mean dietary fiber intake in the UK diet has been measured at 14.7 g/d for men (aged 19–64) and 12.8 g/d for women (aged 19–64) respectively (measured as non-starch polysaccharide). Even the lowest supplementation levels used in animal studies represent a comparable substantial increase above habitual dietary fiber intake in humans.

span.label: critiques → the human SCFA literature, on the ground that it rests on association rather than intervention and on stool output rather than production
span.quote: However, high-level evidence from controlled human trials supporting SCFA as key regulation factors in human metabolism is largely lacking and there is significant reliance on associative studies, rather than interventional studies.

span.label: extends → the seminal sudden-death-victim measurements of SCFA across the gut epithelium and liver, which this review turns into a general principle about tissue exposure
span.quote: The seminal work in sudden-death victims was first to highlight the significant reduction in butyrate, relative to acetate and propionate across the gut epithelium and also the significant reduction in propionate relative to acetate across the liver in humans.

span.label: cross-talk —same-as→ molecular signaling
span.note: the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: 3) improvements in our understanding of the intricate molecular signaling (referred to as “cross-talk”) between the gut microbiome and the host.

span.label: propionate —distinct-from→ acetate
span.note: differs in: metabolic fate in the liver: gluconeogenesis against lipogenesis · the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.95
span.quote: In the liver, propionate is gluconeogenic while acetate and butyrate are lipogenic.

span.label: energy harvesting —contrasted-with→ high-fiber diets
span.note: differs in: direction of the predicted effect of fermentation on body weight · the relation itself is separately evidenced · strength of the relation: 0.9
span.quote: A number of studies have advanced the “energy harvesting” hypothesis, whereby SCFA are thought to contribute additional calories through fermentation in the obese as an explanation for additional weight gain. However, this is not supported by the observational evidence in humans where high-fiber diets, which would be expected to increase SCFA production, protect against weight gain.

span.term: SCFA production cannot be measured directly in humans and stool SCFA output, the measurement used instead, is of unestablished adequacy as a proxy for luminal production
span.quote: The field has been hampered by a lack of methodology to measure SCFA production directly in human studies, although recent work suggests that stable isotope techniques may hold promise. 18 Observations in humans have largely relied on the measurement of stool SCFA output, although it is unclear whether stool SCFA output is a suitable proxy for luminal SCFA production.

span.label: the animal fibre doses behind the SCFA mechanisms translate to 20.9-83.7 g/d for men, against a measured habitual UK intake of 14.7 g/d - even the lowest animal dose is a substantial increase over what people eat
span.term: the animal fibre doses behind the SCFA mechanisms translate to 20.9-83.7 g/d for men, against a measured habitual UK intake of 14.7 g/d - even the lowest animal dose is a substantial increase over what people eat
span.quote: Thus translating the fiber supplementation rates from animal experiments, a daily fiber supplementation in the range 20.9 – 83.7 g/d for men and 16.3 – 65.3 g/d of dietary fiber would be broadly comparable with the 5 – 20% w/w diet loadings used in animal studies. Also from UK NDNS data, mean dietary fiber intake in the UK diet has been measured at 14.7 g/d for men (aged 19–64) and 12.8 g/d for women (aged 19–64) respectively (measured as non-starch polysaccharide). Even the lowest supplementation levels used in animal studies represent a comparable substantial increase above habitual dietary fiber intake in humans.

span.label: SCFA exposure falls along a gradient from lumen to periphery, so an SCFA effect is a different quantity in every tissue and cannot be stated for SCFA as a class
span.term: SCFA exposure falls along a gradient from lumen to periphery, so an SCFA effect is a different quantity in every tissue and cannot be stated for SCFA as a class
span.quote: There is a strong biological gradient for each SCFA from the gut lumen to the periphery which leads to differing cell and tissue SCFA exposure

span.label: a small number of organisms - F. prausnitzii, E. rectale, E. hallii, R. bromii - are responsible for the major fraction of butyrate production
span.term: a small number of organisms - F. prausnitzii, E. rectale, E. hallii, R. bromii - are responsible for the major fraction of butyrate production
span.quote: A surprisingly small number of organisms, dominated by _Faecalibacterium prausnitzii, Eubacterium rectale, Eubacterium hallii and R. bromii_, appear to be responsible for the major fraction of butyrate production.

span.label: the energy-harvesting explanation for obesity is not supported by human observational evidence, where high-fibre diets protect against weight gain
span.term: the energy-harvesting explanation for obesity is not supported by human observational evidence, where high-fibre diets protect against weight gain
span.quote: A number of studies have advanced the “energy harvesting” hypothesis, whereby SCFA are thought to contribute additional calories through fermentation in the obese as an explanation for additional weight gain. However, this is not supported by the observational evidence in humans where high-fiber diets, which would be expected to increase SCFA production, protect against weight gain.

span.label: the paper's own conclusion is conditional: whether the diet-microbiome-metabolism axis can be manipulated to clinical effect is unsettled, and probiotic trials have been unconvincing in metabolic health and weight management
span.term: the paper's own conclusion is conditional: whether the diet-microbiome-metabolism axis can be manipulated to clinical effect is unsettled, and probiotic trials have been unconvincing in metabolic health and weight management
span.quote: _Can the microbiota and its function be manipulated in a predictable way to have a clinically relevant impact on disease risk?_ The answer to this is highly likely to be yes, but probiotic studies designed to change microbiota diversity have been far from convincing in terms of outcome measures in metabolic health 92 and weight management. Prebiotics have had varying degrees of success and the lesson from animal feeding studies may be that high doses of NDC are needed in Western populations to drive physiologically relevant changes in SCFA in order to induce a physiologically relevant effect. This presents a major challenge to translating effective treatments into clinical practice or into strategies that improve population health.

span.label: the primary end-products of fermentation of non-digestible carbohydrates available to the gut microbiota, and the major flow of carbon from diet through microbiome to host
span.quote: Short chain fatty acids (SCFA) are the primary end-products of fermentation of non-digestible carbohydrates (NDC) that become available to the gut microbiota. They represent the major flow of carbon from the diet, through the microbiome to the host.

span.label: butyrate induces proliferation in healthy colonocytes but terminal differentiation and apoptosis in transformed cells - a dual role the field has named
span.quote: Butyrate appears to have a dual role, sometimes referred to as the “butyrate paradox” whereby it induces proliferation in healthy colonocytes but terminal differentiation and apoptosis in transformed cells.

span.label: the proposal that SCFA contribute additional calories through fermentation in the obese, offered as an explanation for additional weight gain
span.quote: A number of studies have advanced the “energy harvesting” hypothesis, whereby SCFA are thought to contribute additional calories through fermentation in the obese as an explanation for additional weight gain. However, this is not supported by the observational evidence in humans where high-fiber diets, which would be expected to increase SCFA production, protect against weight gain.

span.label: g/d, mean dietary fibre intake for UK men aged 19-64, against a 20.9-83.7 g/d animal-equivalent supplementation range
span.quote: Thus translating the fiber supplementation rates from animal experiments, a daily fiber supplementation in the range 20.9 – 83.7 g/d for men and 16.3 – 65.3 g/d of dietary fiber would be broadly comparable with the 5 – 20% w/w diet loadings used in animal studies. Also from UK NDNS data, mean dietary fiber intake in the UK diet has been measured at 14.7 g/d for men (aged 19–64) and 12.8 g/d for women (aged 19–64) respectively (measured as non-starch polysaccharide). Even the lowest supplementation levels used in animal studies represent a comparable substantial increase above habitual dietary fiber intake in humans.

span.label: mg/kg/day of propionate for an 85 kg human, against endogenous glucose production of 2.2 mg/kg/min of which about 50% is gluconeogenic
span.quote: From stoichiometric equations of daily SCFA production from dietary fiber intake, 42 daily propionate production, estimated to be 29.5 mg/kg/day for an average 85 kg human, is likely to make only a relatively small contribution to endogenous glucose production (2.2 mg/kg/min 43) of which approximately 50% may be attributable to gluconeogenesis.

span.label: per cent - the estimated gut-microbiota-derived share of whole-body acetate flux, with the effect of different NDCs on that share largely unknown
span.quote: The contribution of exogenous (gut microbiota derived) acetate production to whole-body acetate flux has been estimated to be approximately 44% 65 but how this proportional contribution is affected by different NDCs and microbiome activity is largely unknown.

span.label: per cent reduction in serum free fatty acids after rectal infusion of acetate and propionate
span.quote: Rectal infusion of acetate and propionate has demonstrated a 40% reduction in serum FFA.

span.label: g/d of supplemented fibre, about 5-10% of dry matter intake, needed to induce appetite-regulation effects in the human studies that found them
span.quote: Supplementation of habitual fiber intake in the range 16 – 35 g/d (approximately 5 – 10 % DMI) is necessary to induce these effects and may reflect the more consistent findings in animals at these equivalent fiber loadings and above.

span.label: normal range
span.quote: High circulating concentrations of SCFA (>1mmol/L; normal range, 0–5 μmol/L for propionate and butyrate), other than acetate, are observed in acidaemic disease in humans and have profound impacts on metabolism because of the toxicity of these organic acids at high concentrations.

span.label: dietary fibre supplementation
span.quote: Animal studies which use dietary fiber supplementation to manipulate colonic SCFA tend to use relatively high fiber supplementation; 5 – 20% w/w NDC in animal dry matter intake (DMI).

span.label: tissue
span.quote: These observations suggest that the roles of SCFA should be considered in each cell or tissue type within this biological gradient. The interplay between epithelial utilization and integrity, splanchnic utilization and peripheral availability requires delineation to determine whether increased production of all SCFA, or selective increases in individual SCFA at specific tissues, determines some of the observed metabolic effects.

span.label: stool SCFA output
span.quote: The field has been hampered by a lack of methodology to measure SCFA production directly in human studies, although recent work suggests that stable isotope techniques may hold promise. 18 Observations in humans have largely relied on the measurement of stool SCFA output, although it is unclear whether stool SCFA output is a suitable proxy for luminal SCFA production.
